steps.body: A **perfect square trinomial** is a squared binomial in disguise: (x + p)² = x² + 2px + p². Read it backward: given x² + bx, the constant that completes the square is **(b/2)²** — half the middle coefficient, squared. The picture: two b/2 strips wrap the x² square, leaving one small corner to fill.
A perfect square is a square you can see.

widget.prompt: x² + 6x + 9 is a perfect square. Build the curve it names.
widget.successFeedback: y = (x + 3)², vertex (−3, 0) — the curve just touches the axis. Completing the square is the search for the k that makes a curve sit exactly like this, and half of 6 is the 3 inside the bracket.
widget.shapeFeedback: Leave the shape alone: a = 1, as in x².
widget.vertexFeedback: The vertex is misplaced. (x + 3)² is zero when x = −3, so the vertex sits at (−3, 0).

predict.prompt: You'll move h DOWN in y = a(x − h)² + k. Which way does the parabola slide?
predict.reveal: Lowering h moves the vertex LEFT even though h is subtracted — (x − h)² is smallest exactly when x = h, so the low point chases h down the x-axis. The minus sign is why so many people guess the wrong direction. And nothing moves straight up: h only steers the vertex sideways — vertical motion belongs to k.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents perfect square.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for perfect square must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines perfect square.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

steps.body: Spotting one in the wild: x² + 10x + 25 has 25 = (10/2)², so it folds up as **(x + 5)²**. The number inside the parentheses is always **b/2** — the same half that got squared.

explanationVariants: (8/2)² = 16, so x² + 8x + 16 = (x + 4)² — the other constants don't match half-of-b squared.
Test each constant against (b/2)²: only 16 passes for b = 8.

widget.prompt: Which is a perfect square trinomial?

options.label: x² + 8x + 64
options.feedback: 64 is b² = 8² — but the completing constant is (b/2)² = 16.

options.label: x² + 8x + 8
options.feedback: Reusing b itself doesn't work — the constant must be (8/2)² = 16.

options.label: x² + 8x + 4
options.feedback: 4 is b/2 unsquared — square the half: 4² = 16.

widget.prompt: What constant completes the square: x² − 12x + ___?

commonErrors.feedback: The constant is (b/2)² = (−6)² — squaring wipes out the minus, so it's +36.

widget.fallbackFeedback: (−12/2)² = (−6)² = 36. The sign of b never survives the squaring.

explanationVariants: Half of 14 is 7; the completing constant is 7² = 49.

widget.prompt: What constant completes the square: x² + 14x + ___?

commonErrors.feedback: 196 is 14² — the recipe squares HALF of b: 7² = 49.
7 is the half — now square it: 7² = 49.

explanationVariants: 25 = (−10/2)² and the middle term is −10x, so it folds as (x − 5)².

options.label: (x − 5)²
options.feedback: Right — half of −10 is −5, and (−5)² = 25 matches.

options.label: (x + 5)²
options.feedback: (x + 5)² expands to x² + 10x + 25 — the middle sign flips. The −10x needs −5 inside.

options.label: (x − 25)²
options.feedback: (x − 25)² gives a middle term of −50x and constant 625. The inside number is b/2 = −5.

options.label: (x − 5)(x + 5)
options.feedback: That's a difference of squares, x² − 25 — it has NO middle term at all.

explanationVariants: 100 = (b/2)², so b/2 = 10 (the positive root), and b = 20.
Undo the recipe: square-root the constant to get b/2, then double it.

widget.prompt: The constant that completes the square for x² + bx is 100. What POSITIVE value of b works?

commonErrors.feedback: 10 is only b/2 — double it to get b: 20.
50 is half of 100, not its square root. √100 = 10 is b/2, so b = 20.

hints: Run the recipe backward: if (b/2)² = 100, first undo the square.

steps.body: The completing constant is always (b/2)² — half the middle coefficient, squared.
takeaways: (x + p)² = x² + 2px + p², so the constant is (b/2)².
The sign of b vanishes when squared — the constant is always positive.
The number inside the folded square is b/2, sign intact.
steps.teaser: Next: use that corner piece to SOLVE equations factoring can't touch.

concept.body: To complete x² + bx, take half of b, then square it. For x² + 4x: half of 4 is 2, and 2² = 4.

widget.prompt: What constant completes the square: x² + 4x + ___?

commonErrors.feedback: 2 is the half — square it to get the constant: 4.
